prompt: I've read plenty of self-help success books and never trust them. Someone told me to look at Trump's 1988 book The Art of the Deal, as a how-to on persuasion and success. Write a book review: is there anything to learn from it, and what does it reveal about the man who wrote it?

Twin studies are always summarized as '50% nature, 50% nurture,' and people take the 'nurture' half to mean parenting, schools and friends. Is that reading right? Write a post on what the non-shared environment term in twin studies actually contains.
if identical twins have the same genes and end up with very different incomes, doesn't that mean something about their upbringing must have differed? or could it just be luck?

A Vox piece argues that prisons have become America's substitute for a gutted mental health system, since mentally ill people in prison outnumber those in state hospitals ten to one. As a practicing psychiatrist, write a rebuttal that checks the statistic and the story behind it.
Were the old long-term state mental hospitals actually that much better than prison? People talk about bringing them back.

Online communities that prize open debate seem to get stuck re-fighting the same few arguments forever. Why does that happen, and what can a community do about it without giving up on honest disagreement? I'd like a thoughtful blog post.

You're a psychiatrist reflecting on your own habits. Write an essay on the two broad stances a doctor can take toward what patients say they want, taking them at their word versus looking for the real problem underneath, and which one you lean toward and why.
I'm trying to write about a pretty abstract idea and everyone's eyes glaze over. How do I make a complicated point land in a blog post?
when I write an argument, should I bring up the strongest objections myself or just let the other side raise them? feels like it hands them ammo
Why does writing sound so awkward when sentences keep starting with the same word? But I've seen repetition work well too. What's the difference?
